from policyengine_uk.model_api import *


class carers_allowance(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "Carer's Allowance"
    documentation = (
        "Carer's Allowance payable after the overlapping-benefit adjustment: "
        "the allowance is reduced by any other personal benefit that overlaps "
        "with it, such as State Pension, and only the balance is paid. The "
        "comparison is made on annual amounts, which equals the weekly rule "
        "when the overlapping benefit is paid at a constant rate all year. "
        "Where the overlapping benefit is above the carer rate in some weeks "
        "and lower or absent in others, for example when it is paid for part "
        "of the year, the annual comparison pays less than the weekly rule "
        "would; annual inputs carry no dates to do better."
    )
    definition_period = YEAR
    unit = GBP
    reference = (
        "https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/70",
        "https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1979/597/regulation/4",
        "https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1979/597/regulation/12",
    )

    def formula(person, period, parameters):
        pre_overlap = person("carers_allowance_pre_overlap", period)
        overlapping = person("carers_allowance_overlapping_benefits", period)
        return max_(pre_overlap - overlapping, 0)

established.interpretation: The default Simulation constructor executes a deterministic UC modifier. It protects seeded existing claimants for 2026–2029, so inspecting uc_LCWRA_element alone would incorrectly claim all claimants are halved. The modifier loops over range(2026,2030), leaving CY2030 outside that protection override. The synthetic observation isolates the cutoff; continued-protection policy scope requires review before calling it an encoding defect.

from policyengine_uk.model_api import Scenario
from policyengine_uk import Microsimulation
from policyengine_uk.utils.data_source import built_from_data
from policyengine_uk.data.economic_assumptions import PROJECTION_END_YEAR
from policyengine_uk.utils.supplied_inputs import set_model_value
import numpy as np
import warnings
from policyengine_core.periods import instant


# Universal Credit Act 2025: the first tax year of the rebalancing (2026-27,
# ss. 2 to 4) and the last the s. 4 duty covers (2029-30).
FIRST_REBALANCING_YEAR = 2026
SECTION_4_LAST_YEAR = 2029
# The tax years in which the scenario sets the element: from the first year of
# the rebalancing to the end of the data's projection. Other code reads this
# (for example to warn that a reform to elements.disabled.amount does not reach
# these years' awards). Later years fall to the uc_LCWRA_element formula, which
# pays every claimant the new-claimant amount.
REBALANCING_YEARS = range(FIRST_REBALANCING_YEAR, PROJECTION_END_YEAR + 1)


# The standard allowance amounts the protected LCWRA amount is paired with in
# the Universal Credit Act 2025 s. 4(2) duty: every amount of the allowance.
STANDARD_ALLOWANCE_TYPES = (
    "SINGLE_YOUNG",
    "SINGLE_OLD",
    "COUPLE_YOUNG",
    "COUPLE_OLD",
)


def protected_lcwra_floor(
    previous_amount: float,
    previous_standard_allowances: dict,
    standard_allowances: dict,
    cpi_factor: float,
) -> float:
    """The lowest protected LCWRA amount the Universal Credit Act 2025 allows.

    s. 4(2): for each standard allowance amount, the protected LCWRA amount
    plus that allowance must be at least the previous tax year's sum,
    increased by the relevant CPI percentage (never below 0%, s. 4(4)(a)). s. 3
    switches off the element's ordinary uprating, so the amount otherwise stays
    where it was. All amounts are monthly.
    """
    factor = max(float(cpi_factor), 1.0)
    required = max(
        (previous_amount + previous_standard_allowances[claimant_type]) * factor
        - standard_allowances[claimant_type]
        for claimant_type in STANDARD_ALLOWANCE_TYPES
    )
    return max(float(previous_amount), required)


def _standard_allowances_monthly(sim: Microsimulation, year: int) -> dict:
    amounts = sim.tax_benefit_system.parameters(
        str(year)
    ).gov.dwp.universal_credit.standard_allowance.amount
    return {
        claimant_type: float(amounts[claimant_type])
        for claimant_type in STANDARD_ALLOWANCE_TYPES
    }


def _relevant_cpi_factor(sim: Microsimulation, year: int) -> float:
    """1 + the relevant CPI percentage for a tax year (UC Act 2025 s. 4(4)(a)):
    the CPI 12-month rate in the September before it. The 0% floor is applied
    in :func:`protected_lcwra_floor`."""
    inputs = sim.tax_benefit_system.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.statutory_uprating_inputs
    return 1 + float(inputs.cpi_september(f"{year - 1}-09-01"))


# The date the fiscal-year annualisation samples a parameter at
# (policyengine_uk.utils.parameters).
FISCAL_YEAR_SAMPLE_DATE = "04-30"


def _protected_amount_parameter(sim: Microsimulation):
    return sim.tax_benefit_system.parameters.gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing.protected_health_element


def _protected_existing_health_element_monthly(
    sim: Microsimulation, year: int
) -> float:
    """The protected LCWRA amount for a tax year, monthly.

    UC Regs 2013 reg. 36 gives one amount to every pre-2026, severe conditions
    criteria or terminally ill claimant, whatever their age or couple status
    (£429.80 for 2026-27, SI 2026/113 reg. 3(3)(b)). Any non-null amount,
    legislated or set by a reform, is used as given. A tax year whose amount
    is null (not yet legislated):

    - to 2029-30 takes the s. 4 floor from the year before;
    - from 2030-31 takes the year before's amount uprated by the element's
      uprating index. The row stays in reg. 36 (s. 2 only relabels it), s. 4
      covers only 2026-27 to 2029-30, and s. 3 disapplies the SSAA 1992
      s. 150 up-rating only in the tax years ending 5 April 2026 to 5 April
      2029, so the review in 2029-30 governs the April 2030 rate again. The
      index is the one the new-claimant amount follows
      (``rebalancing/create_health_element_uprating.py``): the benefit
      uprating index, held in any year the freeze is in force, never falling.
    """
    parameter = _protected_amount_parameter(sim)
    amount = parameter(f"{year}-{FISCAL_YEAR_SAMPLE_DATE}")
    if amount is not None:
        return float(amount)
    first = min(
        int(entry.instant_str[:4])
        for entry in parameter.values_list
        if entry.value is not None
    )
    if year <= first:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No protected LCWRA amount is set for {year} or any earlier year."
        )
    previous = _protected_existing_health_element_monthly(sim, year - 1)
    if year > SECTION_4_LAST_YEAR:
        index = sim.tax_benefit_system.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.indices.uc_health_element
        return previous * (
            index(f"{year}-{FISCAL_YEAR_SAMPLE_DATE}")
            / index(f"{year - 1}-{FISCAL_YEAR_SAMPLE_DATE}")
        )
    return protected_lcwra_floor(
        previous,
        _standard_allowances_monthly(sim, year - 1),
        _standard_allowances_monthly(sim, year),
        _relevant_cpi_factor(sim, year),
    )


NEW_CLAIMANT_STATUS = "uc_receives_new_claimant_health_element"
LCWRA_AMOUNT = "gov.dwp.universal_credit.elements.disabled.amount"


class UCHealthElementOverrideWarning(UserWarning):
    """An LCWRA amount reform is superseded by the rebalancing inputs."""


def warn_shadowed_lcwra_reform(sim) -> None:
    """Warn once when a reformed amount is read in an active rebalancing year.

    Statutory changes are sampled when annualising the LCWRA parameter;
    overrides of the built parameters are read at 1 January. Construction
    and Scenario.apply defer this check until all their changes have run,
    so a reform that also switches rebalancing off does not warn.
    """
    from policyengine_uk.utils.dated_reforms import legacy_override_bounds

    if getattr(sim, "_defer_uc_health_warning", False) or getattr(
        sim, "_uc_health_amount_warning_emitted", False
    ):
        return
    system = getattr(sim, "tax_benefit_system", None)
    if system is None:
        return
    assignments = [
        change
        for change in getattr(system, "dated_assignments", ())
        if change.path == LCWRA_AMOUNT
    ]
    override_windows = [
        legacy_override_bounds(change, system.parameters)
        for change in getattr(system, "legacy_overrides", ())
        if change.path == LCWRA_AMOUNT
    ]
    if not assignments and not override_windows:
        return
    rebalancing = system.parameters.gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing
    years = []
    for year in REBALANCING_YEARS:
        if not rebalancing.active(year):
            continue
        statutory_sample = instant(f"{year}-{FISCAL_YEAR_SAMPLE_DATE}")
        annual_sample = instant(f"{year}-01-01")
        if any(
            change.start <= statutory_sample <= change.stop for change in assignments
        ) or any(start <= annual_sample <= stop for start, stop in override_windows):
            years.append(year)
    if years:
        warnings.warn(
            f"A reform to {LCWRA_AMOUNT} is superseded in "
            f"{', '.join(map(str, years))} by Universal Credit rebalancing inputs. "
            "For a health element reform in these years change "
            "gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing.protected_health_element and "
            "gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing.new_claimant_health_element.",
            UCHealthElementOverrideWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        sim._uc_health_amount_warning_emitted = True


def _new_claimant_health_element_status(
    sim: Microsimulation, year: int, drawn: np.ndarray, built_from_data: bool
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Which benefit units get the new-claimant LCWRA rate in a year.

    A value the situation or dataset supplies is used as given. Data without
    one takes the seeded draw, recorded as an input. A household situation
    without one gets the protected amount (the variable's default): a draw
    there would make a household's award depend on its position among the
    other benefit units in the simulation.
    """
    # sim.get_array reads the simulation's own branch (and the branches it
    # inherits from); the holder's get_array reads only the default branch.
    supplied = sim.get_array(NEW_CLAIMANT_STATUS, year)
    if supplied is not None:
        return np.asarray(supplied, dtype=bool)
    if built_from_data:
        status = np.asarray(drawn, dtype=bool)
    else:
        status = np.zeros(len(drawn), dtype=bool)
    sim.set_input(NEW_CLAIMANT_STATUS, year, status)
    return status


def add_universal_credit_reform(sim: Microsimulation):
    rebalancing = sim.tax_benefit_system.parameters.gov.dwp.universal_credit.rebalancing

    generator = np.random.default_rng(43)

    uc_seed = generator.random(len(sim.calculate("benunit_id")))
    # rebalancing.new_claimant_share: WPI Economics' estimates for 2026-27 to
    # 2029-30, held after that (an assumption; see the parameter).
    new_claimant_share = rebalancing.new_claimant_share
    new_claimant_health_element = rebalancing.new_claimant_health_element
    is_data = built_from_data(sim)
    for year in REBALANCING_YEARS:
        if not rebalancing.active(year):
            continue
        is_post_2025_claimant = _new_claimant_health_element_status(
            sim, year, uc_seed < new_claimant_share(year), is_data
        )
        # Copy: calculate returns the simulation's cached array, and the writes
        # below must reach the cache only through set_input.
        current_health_element = np.array(sim.calculate("uc_LCWRA_element", year))
        has_health_element = current_health_element > 0
        # One protected amount for every pre-2026 claimant (reg. 36).
        current_health_element[has_health_element & ~is_post_2025_claimant] = (
            _protected_existing_health_element_monthly(sim, year) * 12
        )
        # New claimants: £217.26 a month from April 2026 (UC Act 2025 s. 2),
        # frozen to 2029-30 (s. 3) and uprated after.
        current_health_element[has_health_element & is_post_2025_claimant] = (
            new_claimant_health_element(year) * 12
        )  # Monthly amount * 12
        # Stored as an input, so that reforms keep it, but still the model's
        # own element unless one was entered (the benefit cap's LCWRA
        # exception reads entries differently).
        set_model_value(sim, "uc_LCWRA_element", year, current_health_element)

    # The standard allowance uplift is applied through the allowance's
    # uprating index (rebalancing/create_standard_allowance_uprating.py), so a
    # reform to the amount itself is used as given.
    warn_shadowed_lcwra_reform(sim)


universal_credit_july_2025_reform = Scenario(
    simulation_modifier=add_universal_credit_reform,
)

def formula(benunit, period, parameters):
        p = parameters(period).gov.dwp.universal_credit.elements.disabled
        person = benunit.members
        limited_capability = person("uc_limited_capability_for_WRA", period)
        # The element is for "a claimant" with limited capability for work and
        # work-related activity (reg. 27(1)). A partner who cannot be a joint
        # claimant, so that the other member claims as a single person
        # (reg. 3(3)), is not a claimant.
        not_a_claimant = other_member_of_single_claim(person, period)
        person_amounts = (limited_capability & ~not_a_claimant) * p.amount
        return benunit.sum(person_amounts) * MONTHS_IN_YEAR

from policyengine_uk.model_api import *


class ni_class_1_employer(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "NI Class 1 employer-side contributions"
    definition_period = YEAR
    unit = GBP
    defined_for = "ni_class_1_secondary_liable"
    reference = "https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/9"

    def formula(person, period, parameters):
        class_1 = parameters(period).gov.hmrc.national_insurance.class_1
        earnings = person("ni_class_1_income", period)
        if not parameters(
            period
        ).gov.contrib.policyengine.employer_ni.exempt_employer_pension_contributions:
            added_pension_contributions = person(
                "employer_pension_contributions", period
            )
            taxed_earnings = earnings + added_pension_contributions
        else:
            taxed_earnings = earnings
        secondary_threshold = class_1.thresholds.secondary_threshold * WEEKS_IN_YEAR
        main_earnings = max_(
            taxed_earnings - secondary_threshold,
            0,
        )
        return class_1.rates.employer * main_earnings

from policyengine_uk.model_api import *


class adjusted_net_income(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "Adjusted net income"
    documentation = (
        "Income after the gross Gift Aid and relieved pension contribution "
        "adjustments in ITA 2007 s.58. The model's net_income is before "
        "pension relief, so both relieved employee and personal contributions "
        "are deducted here. Pension relief separately enters allowances once "
        "when calculating the income charged to tax."
    )
    definition_period = YEAR
    reference = dict(
        title="Income Tax Act 2007, s. 58",
        href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/58",
    )
    unit = GBP

    def formula(person, period, parameters):
        # s.58 deducts gross Gift Aid and relieved RAS. The model also holds
        # employee contributions gross in net_income, with their relief in
        # allowances, so deduct that relief here too. Taxable-income bases
        # continue to use net_income and allowances: no second deduction.
        return (
            person("net_income", period)
            - person("gift_aid_grossed_up", period)
            - person("pension_contributions_relief", period)
        )

from policyengine_uk.model_api import *


def _top_slice_charge(bottom, top, thresholds, rates, extension):
    """Tax on the slice from ``bottom`` to ``top`` of income, at ``rates``
    between ``thresholds``, every limit above the first raised by
    ``extension``."""
    charge = 0
    for i, rate in enumerate(rates):
        lower = thresholds[i] + (extension if i > 0 else 0)
        upper = thresholds[i + 1] + extension if i + 1 < len(thresholds) else np.inf
        charge = charge + rate * max_(0, min_(top, upper) - max_(bottom, lower))
    return charge


class personal_pension_contributions_tax(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "Pension annual allowance charge"
    documentation = (
        "The annual allowance charge (FA 2004 s. 227) on the chargeable amount, "
        "the pension input amount above the annual allowance. It is charged at "
        "the basic, higher and additional rates on the slices of the chargeable "
        "amount that fall in each band when it is added to the top of the "
        "individual's reduced net income, their income after allowances "
        "(s. 227(4A)-(4B)), with gross Gift Aid extending rate limits. "
        "Relieved relief-at-source contributions extend limits only where "
        "ordinary income, before that relief, meets s. 192(4)/(4A)'s "
        "above-basic-rate condition (s. 227(4C)/(5)). Separate savings rates "
        "from 2017 and UK property rates from 2027 do not satisfy s. 192(4). A Scottish "
        "taxpayer pays the Scottish rates, with the Scottish basic rate on any "
        "slice within the Scottish basic rate limit (s. 227(4AA)). "
        "Personal contribution relief has a separate earnings limit "
        "(pension_contributions_relief); the annual allowance does not "
        "also deny that relief."
    )
    definition_period = YEAR
    reference = [
        dict(
            title="Finance Act 2004 s. 192",
            href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/12/section/192",
        ),
        dict(
            title="Finance Act 2004 s. 227",
            href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/12/section/227",
        ),
        dict(
            title="Income Tax Act 2007 s. 58",
            href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/3/section/58",
        ),
        dict(
            title="Finance Act 2004 s. 233",
            href="https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/12/section/233",
        ),
    ]
    unit = GBP

    def formula(person, period, parameters):
        income_tax = parameters(period).gov.hmrc.income_tax
        rates = income_tax.rates
        chargeable_amount = person("pension_annual_allowance_chargeable_amount", period)
        # FA 2004 s. 227(4B)-(4C): relief at source remains in reduced net
        # income. It raises rate limits only if s. 192's condition is met.
        # The model includes
        # that relief in allowances, so restore it at Step 3. Net pay
        # contributions stay deducted. Gift Aid is already excluded from
        # allowances; only its gross amount extends the limits (ITA 2007
        # s. 414(2)), without another deduction from the taxable base.
        relief_at_source = min_(
            person("personal_pension_contributions", period),
            person("pension_contributions_relief", period),
        )
        gross_gift = person("gift_aid_grossed_up", period)
        allowances_at_step_3 = max_(
            0,
            person("allowances", period) - relief_at_source,
        )
        # Reduced net income is income after ITA 2007 s. 23 Step 3, not
        # adjusted net income after the s. 58 gross Gift Aid deduction.
        reduced_net_income = max_(
            0, person("net_income", period) - allowances_at_step_3
        )
        top_of_charge = reduced_net_income + chargeable_amount

        # s. 192(4): test ordinary liability apart from RAS relief, with
        # Gift Aid's limits still extended. s. 227(5) excludes the pension
        # excess itself. Separate dividend rates, savings rates from 2017
        # (FA 2016 s. 6) and UK property rates from 2027 (FA 2026 s. 6) do not
        # satisfy its named higher/additional-rate condition. Retain the
        # model's fixed allowance allocation, apart from RAS relief.
        savings = person("taxable_savings_interest_income", period)
        dividends = person("taxable_dividend_income", period)
        non_savings = max_(0, reduced_net_income - savings - dividends)
        uk_basic_limit = rates.uk.thresholds[1] + gross_gift
        # Property is stacked above other non-savings income. Its part of
        # this pre-RAS base must use allowances with RAS restored too.
        property_at_separate_rates = min_(
            person("taxable_property_income", period), non_savings
        ) * (period.start.year >= 2027)
        uk_ras_condition = non_savings - property_at_separate_rates > uk_basic_limit
        if period.start.year < 2017:
            # Before separate savings rates, a non-nil higher/additional
            # savings slice was charged at the rates named in s. 192(4).
            savings_top = max_(0, reduced_net_income - dividends)
            savings_after_allowances = savings_top - non_savings
            savings_amounts = income_tax.allowances.personal_savings_allowance
            savings_allowance_without_ras = select(
                [
                    reduced_net_income > rates.uk.thresholds[2] + gross_gift,
                    reduced_net_income > uk_basic_limit,
                ],
                [savings_amounts.additional, savings_amounts.higher],
                default=savings_amounts.basic,
            )
            nil_rate_savings = min_(
                savings_after_allowances,
                savings_allowance_without_ras
                + max_(0, rates.savings_starter_rate.allowance - non_savings),
            )
            uk_ras_condition = uk_ras_condition | (
                savings_top > max_(uk_basic_limit, non_savings + nil_rate_savings)
            )

        uk_charge = _top_slice_charge(
            reduced_net_income,
            top_of_charge,
            list(rates.uk.thresholds),
            list(rates.uk.rates),
            gross_gift + relief_at_source * uk_ras_condition,
        )

        # s. 227(4AA)(b)(i): no slice is charged at the starter rate. The
        # Scottish basic rate applies to every slice up to the Scottish basic
        # rate limit, so charge the starter band at the basic rate. The
        # starter bracket (the first) is null before 2018-19, when the lowest
        # Scottish rate was the basic rate; it is present only with both a
        # rate and a threshold.
        scottish_rates = rates.scotland.rates
        scottish_band_rates = list(scottish_rates.rates)
        starter_bracket = person.simulation.tax_benefit_system.parameters.gov.hmrc.income_tax.rates.scotland.rates.brackets[
            0
        ]
        has_starter_band = (
            starter_bracket.rate(period.start) is not None
            and starter_bracket.threshold(period.start) is not None
            and len(scottish_band_rates) > 1
        )
        if has_starter_band:
            scottish_band_rates[0] = scottish_band_rates[1]
        # s. 192(4A): only non-savings income is charged at Scottish rates.
        # The first rate above basic is intermediate from 2018, higher before.
        scottish_ras_condition = False
        for threshold, rate in zip(scottish_rates.thresholds, scottish_band_rates):
            if rate > scottish_band_rates[0]:
                scottish_ras_condition = scottish_ras_condition | (
                    non_savings > threshold + gross_gift
                )
        scottish_charge = _top_slice_charge(
            reduced_net_income,
            top_of_charge,
            list(scottish_rates.thresholds),
            scottish_band_rates,
            gross_gift + relief_at_source * scottish_ras_condition,
        )

        return where(
            person("pays_scottish_income_tax", period),
            scottish_charge,
            uk_charge,
        )
